articles.headline: RBI to transfer record ₹2.11 lakh crore surplus to Government
articles.summary: The RBI Board approved a record surplus transfer of ₹2,10,874 crore to the Union Government for FY24. This is 141% higher than the previous year's transfer of ₹87,416 crore. The windfall is expected to help the government meet its fiscal deficit target of 5.1% of GDP for FY25 and potentially increase capital expenditure on infrastructure projects.

articles.headline: Sensex and Nifty hit record highs following RBI dividend boost
articles.summary: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty touched fresh all-time highs on Thursday after the RBI announced a much higher-than-expected dividend transfer. The Sensex surged over 1,100 points, crossing the 75,000 mark, while the Nifty neared 23,000. Banking and financial stocks led the rally as the news bolstered investor sentiment regarding India's fiscal health.

articles.headline: UK PM Rishi Sunak calls for General Election on July 4
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak has officially announced a snap general election to be held on July 4, 2024. Addressing the nation from Downing Street, Sunak highlighted economic stability and invited voters to choose their future path. The announcement sets the stage for a six-week campaign as the Conservative Party currently trails the Labour Party in major polls.

articles.headline: Nvidia revenue jumps 262 percent on massive AI chip demand
articles.summary: Nvidia reported a staggering 262% year-over-year increase in Q1 revenue to $26 billion, driven by demand for AI chips. Net income rose over 600% to $14.88 billion. The company also announced a 10-for-1 stock split and raised its quarterly dividend by 150%, reflecting its dominant position as the primary hardware supplier for the global artificial intelligence boom.

articles.headline: IndiGo Q4 profit doubles to ₹1,895 crore as travel demand surges
articles.summary: InterGlobe Aviation, operator of IndiGo, reported a net profit of ₹1,895 crore for the fourth quarter, up from ₹919 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations increased by 26% to ₹17,825 crore. Despite higher fuel costs and ongoing engine issues grounded aircraft, strong passenger growth and improved capacity utilization fueled the airline's record performance.

articles.headline: North India heatwave pushes peak power demand to record 233 GW
articles.summary: A severe heatwave across Northern India has pushed the country's peak power demand to a record 233.79 GW. Temperatures reached 48°C in parts of Rajasthan and 47°C in Delhi, leading to high cooling loads. The Ministry of Power expects demand to stay elevated, while the IMD has issued red alerts for several states, warning of continued extreme heat conditions.

articles.headline: SEBI eases material change disclosure timelines for foreign investors
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has approved a proposal to provide Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) more time to disclose material changes. FPIs will now have seven working days to report material changes and 30 days to provide supporting documents. The move is intended to reduce the compliance burden and simplify operational procedures for foreign funds.

articles.headline: Awfis Space Solutions IPO subscribed 4.28 times on second day
articles.summary: The initial public offering of coworking space provider Awfis Space Solutions received strong response, being subscribed 4.28 times on day two. The retail portion saw 12.25 times subscription, while non-institutional investors bid 6.84 times their quota. The company aims to raise ₹599 crore to fund capital expenditure for new centers and for general corporate purposes.

articles.headline: UGC allows direct PhD entry for four-year undergraduate degree holders
articles.summary: The University Grants Commission (UGC) has announced that students with a four-year undergraduate degree and a minimum of 75% marks can now directly apply for PhD programs. This eliminates the mandatory requirement for a Master's degree for such candidates. The decision aligns with the National Education Policy 2020 to streamline academic pathways and promote research.

articles.headline: Garden Reach Shipbuilders reports 33 percent growth in Q4 profit
articles.summary: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) reported a 33% increase in net profit to ₹111.6 crore for the quarter ended March 31, 2024. Revenue from operations jumped 69% year-on-year to ₹1,016 crore. The board recommended a final dividend of ₹1.44 per equity share. The growth was attributed to strong execution in shipbuilding and increased order book visibility.

articles.headline: Southwest Monsoon expected to hit Kerala coast by May 31
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast that the southwest monsoon is likely to arrive over Kerala on May 31, 2024. This early onset is seen as a positive sign for the agricultural sector, which relies on the June-September rains for nearly 70% of the country's rainfall. Adequate rainfall is crucial for controlling food inflation and boosting rural demand.

articles.headline: Nykaa parent FSN E-Commerce reports 187 percent rise in profit
articles.summary: FSN E-Commerce Ventures, parent of Nykaa, reported a consolidated net profit of ₹9.07 crore for Q4 FY24, nearly triple from ₹3.16 crore in the year-ago period. Total revenue from operations grew 28% to ₹1,668 crore. The company cited strong demand in the beauty and personal care segments and improved operational efficiencies for the sharp increase in profitability.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues contempt notice to TN in Deepam row
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued a contempt notice to the Tamil Nadu government for allegedly defying orders regarding the Deepam festival at Arunachaleswarar temple. The court noted that authorities brazenly disobeyed its November 20 directive. It directed the state to permit the lighting of a ceremonial lamp atop the hill under specific security conditions.

articles.headline: Sitting or retired SC judge to head delimitation commission
articles.summary: The proposed delimitation bill mandates a three-member commission chaired by a serving or retired Supreme Court judge. Other members include the Chief Election Commissioner or an EC nominee and the state's election commissioner. The commission will have the power of a civil court and will redraft constituency boundaries based on census figures.

articles.headline: Census 2027 to begin with online enumeration from January 10
articles.summary: The Indian government has notified that the enumeration for Census 2027 will begin on January 10. Residents will have a 15-day window for self-enumeration through an online portal. The house-to-house population count is scheduled from March 1 to March 5, 2027. This marks the first digital census in India's history.

articles.headline: Rohit Sharma returns as Mumbai Indians captain after three seasons
articles.summary: Mumbai Indians have reinstated Rohit Sharma as captain for the IPL 2027 season. Rohit, who led the team to five titles, replaces Hardik Pandya. The decision follows three seasons where the team struggled to find consistency. Team owners expressed confidence that Rohit's leadership would help reclaim their former glory in the tournament.

articles.headline: Delhi government spent 37.4% of budget in first seven months
articles.summary: Data shows the Delhi government utilized 23,391 crore, or 37.4% of its 62,550 crore allocation, between April and October 2026. The department of industries saw the lowest expenditure at 2.07%, while the energy department spent the highest proportion at 77.98%. Officials cited slow progress in some sectors but expect spending to pick up in the second half.

articles.headline: Safdarjung Hospital denies claims of hiring doctor with fake degrees
articles.summary: Safdarjung Hospital authorities denied allegations that they knowingly hired a doctor with fake MBBS and MD degrees. The individual, identified as Ramkishor Mahawar, allegedly worked on a contractual basis using forged documents. The hospital stated it follows due diligence and is cooperating with the police investigation into the matter.

articles.headline: UP Lok Sabha seats could reach 600 plus under delimitation
articles.summary: Projections under the new delimitation bill suggest that Uttar Pradesh's Lok Sabha seats could increase from 80 to over 600. The plan proposes a 50% uniform increase across all states and union territories. Critics from southern states have expressed concern that this could lead to political marginalization of regions with successful population control.

articles.headline: ECI fixes security flaw that exposed voter data on website
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India fixed a vulnerability on its website that potentially exposed personal details of millions of voters. Security researchers discovered that the site allowed access to sensitive data via predictable URL patterns. ECI officials stated that no data was misused and that secondary security layers have been implemented to prevent future risks.

articles.headline: CDS warns of space threat as Pakistan gains China's backing
articles.summary: Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan warned that Pakistan's space capabilities, supported by China, pose a growing challenge to India's security. He emphasized the need for India to strengthen its own space assets and integrate them with military operations. He noted that the nature of future conflicts would be increasingly multi-domain.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy calls for more US pressure on Putin to end war
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the United States to increase pressure on Russian President Vladimir Putin to negotiate an end to the conflict. In an interview, he compared Putin to Hitler and stated that only strong international intervention could stop the aggression. He expressed hope for continued support from the incoming US administration.

articles.headline: New Zealand leads as India misses early chances in Test
articles.summary: New Zealand reached 246/5 on the opening day of the second Test against India in Christchurch. Indian bowlers, led by Akash Deep, struggled to capitalize on early opportunities as Tom Latham and Tom Blundell struck fifties. India's fielding was criticized for dropping crucial catches that allowed the hosts to build a solid platform.

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs food regulators to implement health warning labels
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ordered the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to finalize a system for health warning labels on packaged foods. The court emphasized that consumers have a right to clear information about high sugar, salt, and fat content. FSSAI must now revise its nutrient limits and finish the framework within four months.

articles.headline: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat share until 2051
articles.summary: The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill proposes extending the freeze on inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for 25 years to 2051. Accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, it seeks to increase the number of seats in each State by 50%, raising the total Lower House strength from 550 to 850. This move also triggers the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.

articles.headline: DMK stands firm on demands regarding seat share and Census
articles.summary: DMK chief M.K. Stalin reiterated that the party will not compromise on two key demands: protecting Tamil Nadu's current 7.18% Lok Sabha seat share and freezing State seat proportions based on the 1971 Census for another 25 years. The party has consistently opposed delimitation based on more recent population figures that would disadvantage States with successful family planning.

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders ceremonial lamp lighting at Thirupparankundram deepathoon
articles.summary: Rejecting the Tamil Nadu government's claims, the Supreme Court ordered the Karthigai Deepam to be lit on the stone pillar atop Thirupparankundram Hill. The court observed 'wilful disobedience' of its prior order and issued show cause notices to top State officials. Receivers were appointed to oversee the ceremony, with Central forces providing security during the event on Saturday.

articles.headline: Indian Navy receives final Project 17A stealth frigate Vindhyagiri
articles.summary: The Indian Navy took delivery of Vindhyagiri, the seventh and final ship of the Nilgiri-class Project 17A stealth frigates, from Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers in Kolkata. The multi-mission platform features 75% indigenous content and advanced weaponry for anti-surface, anti-air, and anti-submarine warfare, marking a milestone in India's warship construction capabilities.

articles.headline: Hackers breach U.S. military flagship cloud computing platform
articles.summary: The U.S. Air Force's Cloud One platform has been breached, potentially compromising sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data. The intrusion was discovered during a system upgrade. Cloud One serves as a centralized IT hub powered by major tech providers, managing applications including air defense radar data feeds and combat munitions tracking systems across 200 locations.

articles.headline: Early-life sugar restrictions linked to significantly lower cancer risk
articles.summary: A study of wartime sugar rationing in the U.K. found that reducing sugar exposure during the first 1,000 days of life is associated with a 36% to 69% lower risk of several cancers later in adulthood. Research published in PNAS suggests early-life restrictions slow biological aging by 2.2 years and establish healthier long-term eating habits through behavioral and biological pathways.

articles.headline: Delhi government opens Kejriwal's former residence for public tour
articles.summary: The Delhi government opened 6, Flagstaff Road, dubbed 'Sheesh Mahal' by the BJP, to the media ahead of its public launch. The bungalow, where Arvind Kejriwal stayed as CM until October 2024, features a living room lounge built at a cost of ₹1.48 crore and ₹1.07 crore worth of drapes. Central agencies are currently investigating alleged irregularities in the property's construction.

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court sets aside appointment of Bengal LoP
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court quashed the West Bengal Speaker’s June 3 decision to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of the Opposition. Justice Krishna Rao ruled the appointment unsustainable under law following a split in the Trinamool Congress and allegations of forged signatures. The Speaker has been directed to reconsider the appointment afresh within 10 days.

articles.headline: Delhi and Bihar sign pact for 18 inter-State bus routes
articles.summary: Delhi and Bihar have agreed to operate inter-State bus services connecting the national capital with 13 destinations in Bihar, including Patna, Gaya, and Purnia. The agreement is expected to benefit 20 lakh people, including students and workers. Fares for the new services, operated under a public-private partnership model, are expected to range from ₹2,000 to ₹3,000.

articles.headline: Delhi government develops app to track faulty streetlights
articles.summary: A new mobile application is being tested by Delhi Police to map dark spots and route streetlight maintenance complaints to the correct civic agency in real time. Developed by Geospatial Delhi Limited, the app captures location coordinates to reduce jurisdictional confusion. Police have already identified 180 dark spots and over 5,000 defective streetlights across the city.

articles.headline: MCD adds 10 mechanical sweepers to tackle Delhi air pollution
articles.summary: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta flagged off 10 mechanical road sweepers, bringing the Municipal Corporation of Delhi's fleet to 76. The move aims to combat winter air pollution caused by road dust. Each machine can clean 40 lane-kilometres per shift. The MCD plans to expand the fleet to 136 machines by July to increase daily coverage from 2,100 to 5,000 lane-kilometres.

articles.headline: H.P. BJP demands re-exam for Sikh youth barred over kara
articles.summary: The Himachal Pradesh BJP Minority Morcha has sought a re-examination for a patwari post after an Amritdhari Sikh candidate was allegedly barred from the exam for wearing a 'kara' and 'kirpan'. The party called the incident a violation of religious freedom and constitutional rights, demanding a formal probe and an explanation from the State government.

articles.headline: Congress maintains lead in Rajasthan rural local body elections
articles.summary: The Opposition Congress emerged dominant in Rajasthan's panchayati raj elections, securing 255 pradhan posts out of 419 rural bodies. The ruling BJP won 105 seats, while the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party secured 24 posts. Congress won clear leads in 25 of 37 districts, including 16 of 22 panchayat samitis in Jaipur district, despite the BJP's State-level governance.

articles.headline: TVK MLA Arul Vignesh arrested for harassing woman IAS officer
articles.summary: Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested for allegedly making inappropriate advances and comments toward a woman IAS officer. The arrest followed a Madras High Court directive to investigate the complaint. Police served a summons at his residence before taking him into custody for interrogation at the local Circuit House.

articles.headline: J&K leaders condemn police summons to cleric over Vande Mataram
articles.summary: Kashmir political leaders, including Mirwaiz Umar Farooq and Mehbooba Mufti, condemned the police for summoning Maulana Rehmatullah Qasimi. The cleric had opposed the playing of Vande Mataram at a recent J&K Waqf Board event, calling it 'un-Islamic'. Leaders termed the summons an attempt to intimidate religious voices and suppress dissent within the Union Territory.

articles.headline: Telangana to issue land passbooks with embedded maps
articles.summary: The Telangana government is preparing to issue first-of-its-kind pattadar passbooks featuring embedded maps and land coordinates. The new design includes a unique QR-style code that provides digital information about the specific plot. The initiative follows a phased resurvey of 10,900 revenue villages and aims to create a comprehensive digital land registry for farmers.

articles.headline: UPPSC PCS preliminary results set aside over reservation errors
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court cancelled the PCS-2025 preliminary results, ruling that the UPPSC wrongly excluded meritorious reserved-category candidates from the unreserved list. The court directed the commission to redraw the merit list and conduct the mains examination afresh. This follows findings that thousands of OBC, SC, and EWS candidates outscored unreserved candidates.

articles.headline: Bangladesh unrest shifts global textile orders toward Indian hubs
articles.summary: Global fashion giants including Zara and H&M have moved nearly 10% of monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian hubs, primarily India, due to ongoing labor unrest. Political uncertainty and energy shortages in Bangladesh have caused over $400 million in production losses, eroding the country's competitive edge in the apparel export market.

articles.headline: Trump urges Putin to end military aggression in Europe
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated he asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to 'pull back all military aggression' against European territories during their meeting in China. In a shift in tone, Trump expressed hope for a quick deal between Russia and Ukraine. The comments come as European nations voice increasing concern over potential Russian provocations beyond Ukraine.

articles.headline: China military tests makeshift floating bridges for Taiwan landing
articles.summary: Satellite imagery reveals the People's Liberation Army is conducting amphibious landing drills in Fujian province, testing methods to link civilian vessels into makeshift floating bridges. Experts suggest the exercise rehearses low-signature logistical support for a potential invasion scenario. The drills in Dacheng Bay have been ongoing since early November.

articles.headline: Gukesh shows resilience in World Chess Championship draws
articles.summary: D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov remain tied 7-7 after three games of the World Chess Championship in Geneva. Gukesh demonstrated high-level preparation and defensive skill, particularly in Game 3 where he equalized easily with the black pieces. The match, consisting of 14 classical games, will proceed to shorter tie-break formats if the score remains level.

articles.headline: James Gray returns to crime thriller genre with Paper Tiger
articles.summary: Director James Gray returns to the crime thriller genre with his new film Paper Tiger. The movie follows a New York family that becomes entangled with the Russian mafia. The production features a high-profile cast including Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson, and Michael Teller, and is currently showing in theatres.

articles.headline: Archaeologists discover international stir in new series Dig
articles.summary: The new comedy series Dig, created by Amy Poehler and Michael Schur, follows archaeologists working in Greece who uncover a discovery that causes an international sensation. The show features Amy Poehler in a starring role alongside Hugh Laurie and is available for streaming on JioHotstar.

articles.headline: Qutub Minar to host Candlelight Open Air musical tribute
articles.summary: A Candlelight Open Air concert at Delhi's Qutub Minar will feature a musical tribute to composer A.R. Rahman. The event, held in collaboration with Sabhyata Foundation, will showcase instrumental renditions of famous compositions like Jiya Jale and Masakali performed by the Indian classical ensemble KMA Trio.

articles.headline: Documentary follows Elizabeth Holmes before jail sentence
articles.summary: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary, You Can See Everything, chronicles Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in the final weeks before she began her jail sentence. The film explores her perspective after being convicted of defrauding the public through her failed medical company.

articles.headline: Blade Runner franchise expands with new television series
articles.summary: The Blade Runner franchise is launching its first television series titled Blade Runner 2099. Created by Silka Luisa and starring Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer, the project follows the cinematic entries directed by Ridley Scott and Denis Villeneuve. It is currently streaming on Amazon Prime.

articles.headline: World War II football players featured in The Mosquito Bowl
articles.summary: The Mosquito Bowl follows four college football players who enlist in the US Marines and play a final game before the Battle of Okinawa during World War II. The Netflix series stars Nicholas Galitzine and Bill Skarsgård, focusing on the intersection of sport and military history.

articles.headline: Abhishek Pathak directs police procedural Drishyam: The Conclusion
articles.summary: The third instalment of the Hindi crime series, Drishyam: The Conclusion, is now streaming on Netflix. Directed by Abhishek Pathak and starring Ajay Devgn, Tabu, and Jaideep Ahlawat, the film follows protagonist Vijay Salgaonkar as he continues to protect his family from long-standing murder charges.

articles.headline: Ritesh Meshram explores everyday objects in Metalmorphosis solo show
articles.summary: Artist Ritesh Meshram’s solo exhibition, Metalmorphosis, is on display at Mumbai’s Chemould Prescott Road. The show features sculptures that repurpose everyday metal objects into art, reflecting Meshram's background in the industrial environment of Bhilai and his training in fine arts and theatre.

articles.headline: Modern wellness culture creates burnout through habit stacking
articles.summary: The trend of habit-stacking in modern wellness culture is increasingly leading to exhaustion. While adding small healthy behaviors to daily routines is intended to simplify lifestyle changes, many individuals find the growing list of daily supplements, training, and step-count goals overwhelming.

articles.headline: Vivo X Fold6 aims to eliminate foldable smartphone compromises
articles.summary: The Vivo X Fold6 seeks to compete with traditional flagship smartphones by addressing common weaknesses in foldable hardware. The device focuses on improving camera quality and battery life, which are often reduced in folding designs, to provide a high-end experience without technical trade-offs.

articles.headline: Cocktail coats and embellished blazers trend in occasion wear
articles.summary: Statement layering is becoming a centerpiece of contemporary fashion, with designers like Tarun Tahiliani and Falguni Shane Peacock popularizing cocktail coats. Embellished long-line jackets and beaded capelets are being used in wedding and festive wear to add structure and couture artistry.

articles.headline: Practical ways to turn exercise warm-ups into workouts
articles.summary: Fitness experts suggest that warm-up routines can be made more productive by treating them as additional training rather than a chore. By incorporating resistance and specific movements like toe taps and push-ups, athletes can improve physical preparedness and mental focus before their main session.

articles.headline: Lucknow artisans revive century-old chatapati craft for modern fashion
articles.summary: Artisans in Lucknow are adapting the traditional chatapati-ka-kaam craft for contemporary tastes. The technique, which involves piecing together silk fragments and reinforcing them with zardozi, is being used by studios like Sanatkada to create wearable products like saris and cushion covers to preserve the dying skill.

articles.headline: Psychological impact of the November-December liminal period
articles.summary: The period between Diwali and the New Year is often experienced as a 'liminal space' characterized by emotional ambiguity. Psychotherapists observe that while year-end festivities offer temporary relief, the shift in routines can also stir anxiety about unaccomplished goals and future transitions.

articles.headline: Unreasonable hospitality challenges restaurant walk-in culture
articles.summary: As high-end restaurants increasingly prioritize influencers and digital reservations, the traditional walk-in experience is becoming more difficult. Sociology experts and restaurateurs emphasize that 'unreasonable hospitality'—valuing the customer’s time and humanity—is essential even when tables are unavailable.

articles.headline: Sharon Horgan explores middle-age complexities in new series Youth
articles.summary: Actress and writer Sharon Horgan stars in the new series Youth, streaming on JioHotstar. The show explores themes of aging, motherhood, and dating in one's 50s with dark humor and incisive writing. It features Horgan alongside Aran Murphy and Rupert Friend in a story about navigating life's disappointments.

articles.headline: Supreme Court suspends life sentences in Bilkis Bano case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has suspended the life sentences and granted bail to two convicts in the Bilkis Bano case. Bano, who naming her attackers after facing horrific violence during the 2002 Gujarat riots, is contesting the decision. The ruling raises questions about legal precedents and the rights of survivors.

articles.headline: Forgotten women peace workers of Noakhali riots remembered
articles.summary: The historical role of local women’s groups in restoring peace during the 1946 Noakhali riots is being highlighted. Leaders from various political backgrounds worked under Mahatma Gandhi’s guidance to organize relief and rebuild trust between communities, though their contributions remain largely invisible in national narratives.

articles.headline: Curated objects and entertainment ideas for festive house parties
articles.summary: As the festive season begins, hosts are incorporating specialized items like fluted glass water dispensers and tiered serving stands into their parties. Tech elements like karaoke machines and high-fidelity vinyl record players are also trending to create more interactive and memorable social gatherings.

articles.headline: Expert guidelines for DJing a successful house party
articles.summary: DJ Easymanie shares professional tips for managing music at domestic social events. Key advice includes reading the room to balance high-energy dance tracks with slower ballads, managing song requests politely, and using a variety of genres like 90s Bollywood and modern hip-hop to build a cohesive narrative.

articles.headline: Professionals share minimalist and regional trends in cocktail making
articles.summary: Modern cocktail trends are shifting away from excessive theatre toward cleaner, flavor-led drinks. Mixologists are incorporating regional Indian ingredients like kokum, gondhoraj lime, and mustard oil, while 'batching' drinks in advance is recommended for home hosts to manage hospitality efficiently.

articles.headline: Fashion designers elevate party menus with artistic concepts
articles.summary: Indian fashion designers like Abu Jani, Sandeep Khosla, and Monica Shah are treating party food as an extension of their design aesthetic. From grazing tables that double as decor to regional artisanal snacks and monochrome-themed dishes, culinary offerings at fashion soirées now emphasize heart and provenance.

articles.headline: Traditional Rampur halwa recipes feature unusual ingredients
articles.summary: Historical cookbooks from the former princely state of Rampur reveal unique sweet dishes like adrak (ginger) halwa. Originally created by royal khansamas for medicinal purposes, the complex dish requires hours of cooking and is noted for its sharp, distinctive flavor that is prized in North Indian winter cuisine.

articles.headline: Equity crowdfunding platforms allow diners to invest in restaurants
articles.summary: New investment platforms like Investorant and Hotshare are enabling regular diners to fund restaurant concepts. By pooling capital from private investors for ticket sizes as low as ₹10,000, these platforms aim to support creative talent and expansion while offering investors perks and a share of operating cash flow.

articles.headline: International labels reissue obscure Indian vinyl records for collectors
articles.summary: Obscure Indian music from the 1980s, such as Rupa Biswas’s Disco Jazz, is finding a second life through international reissues. Labels like Numero Group and Naya Beat are restoring rare records that fused traditional Indian sounds with disco and funk, reaching global audiences decades after their initial release.

articles.headline: TeamLab co-founder discusses independence in art and tech
articles.summary: Daisuke Sakai, co-founder of the teamLab art collective, emphasizes the importance of creative independence and collaborative design. In an interview, he discusses how the collective blends digital technology with physical space and why human emotion and physical touch remain vital in an era increasingly dominated by AI.

articles.headline: Manav Kaul’s new play explores self-doubt in creativity
articles.summary: Playwright Manav Kaul’s latest production, Ek Haare Hue Kavi Ki Safal Kavita, examines the internal struggles of a poet. The play depicts the conflict between tradition and modernity, including the impact of artificial intelligence on creative labor, through a dialogue between a poet and his incomplete verses.

articles.headline: Cyclist Mudit Kohli completes 5,000km race in memory of brother
articles.summary: Cyclist Mudit Kohli finished the Transcontinental Race (TCR) across Europe in 18 days, riding in memory of his brother Mohit, who died in a road accident during a world record attempt. The 5,000km self-supported journey from Norway to Greece served as a personal milestone in Kohli's journey through grief.

articles.headline: New generation of Indian women shuttlers gains international recognition
articles.summary: A wave of young Indian women badminton players, including Tanvi Sharma and Rakshitha Sree Ramraj, is rising in the world rankings. With nine players in the top 50, the depth of talent in Indian women's singles is increasing ahead of the 2028 Olympic cycle and a planned shift in the sport's scoring system.

articles.headline: Anjum Hasan’s Shillong memoir paints a cosmopolitan hill town
articles.summary: In her new book, Shillong in the World, author Anjum Hasan explores the diverse identity of the hill town through portraits of its long-term residents. The memoir weaves personal history with accounts of ethnic tensions and cultural connections, presenting a picture of a place defined by both its past and global influences.

articles.headline: Samit Basu’s new novel satirizes the Bollywood writer’s room
articles.summary: The Pictures of Darpan Ray, Samit Basu’s first contemporary fiction novel, offers a dark comedy about youth pursuing careers in Bollywood. Reimagining Oscar Wilde’s Dorian Gray, the book explores the cynicism, narcissism, and artistic compromises found within India's massive film industry.

articles.headline: Domestic equities snap winning streak as investors book profits
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices Nifty 50 and Sensex fell 0.7-0.8% this week, ending a four-week rally. Despite foreign institutional investors buying ₹31,500 crore worth of equities, the market saw consolidation. Information technology was the top-performing sector, while metals faced significant losses.

articles.headline: Shortages of butter and ghee loom as dairy stocks thin
articles.summary: India faces potential shortages of milk fat products like butter and ghee due to weak rainfall and high cattle-feed costs. Dairies, including Amul, have depleted their reserves as milk procurement fell by up to 15% in regions like Maharashtra and Karnataka. Prices for dairy butter rose 54% year-on-year in October.

articles.headline: Companies increase technical oversight of vendors under new data rules
articles.summary: Firms are tightening vendor audits and data storage checks ahead of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act deadline. Under the new regime, data fiduciaries cannot shift legal blame to vendors for breaches. Companies are now ranking vendors by data exposure and demanding stricter security controls.

articles.headline: Indian automakers face rising tax disputes and multibillion-rupee claims
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki, Toyota, and Mercedes-Benz have reported sharp increases in tax disputes involving income tax, GST, and customs duties. These claims, some reaching thousands of crores, create financial uncertainty as companies plan massive investments. Experts warn that lengthy investigations impact the ease of doing business.

articles.headline: UN food agencies warn of worsening hunger in 16 areas
articles.summary: United Nations food agencies have warned that hunger is expected to worsen over the next six months in 16 locations, primarily in Africa. Conflicts in Sudan and Yemen, along with extreme climate events like El Niño, are the primary drivers of acute food insecurity in these regions.

articles.headline: Power minister Manohar Lal urges states to add nuclear capacity
articles.summary: Union power minister Manohar Lal has emphasized the necessity of increasing nuclear power generation to meet India's clean energy goals. Speaking on Friday, he also urged state governments to implement policy measures to stabilize the financial position of power distribution companies.

articles.headline: RBI reduces 2029 bond sale as market anticipates rate hike
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India accepted bids for only 40% of its scheduled 2029 bond sale during a Friday auction. The move aims to keep yields below 7% as market expectations of an interest rate hike on 4 December drive bond yields higher across the banking system.

articles.headline: ICC exceeds sponsorship revenue targets in shortened cycle
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council met and exceeded revenue expectations during its 2024-27 sponsorship cycle. Commercial officer Anurag Dahiya noted strong growth from global partners like Coca-Cola and Aramco. The ICC is seeing increased interest in longer-term eight-year deals from major advertisers.

articles.headline: Companies raise hiring bar on campuses as AI automates roles
articles.summary: recruiters are offering higher pay but hiring fewer candidates this placement season as AI takes over routine junior tasks. Engineering and management students now face tougher assessments focused on decision-making, ethical dilemmas, and specialized skills like machine learning and low-latency research.

articles.headline: Gaganyaan astronauts assist in engineering India’s indigenous spacecraft
articles.summary: The four astronauts chosen for India's Gaganyaan mission are actively contributing to the engineering of the crew module. Utilizing their backgrounds as test pilots, they are helping shape avionics and safety systems for the 2027-28 orbital flight, which aims to establish India as a global player in human spaceflight.

articles.headline: Kotak leads ECM league following marquee IPO mandates
articles.summary: Kotak Mahindra Capital Co. has emerged as a top player in India's equity capital markets, securing mandates for major IPOs like Jio Platforms and the NSE. The homegrown bank has generated $160 million in revenue since 2024, competing successfully against global Wall Street heavyweights in deal volume and fees.

articles.headline: Sebi clears Sterlite Electric and seven other firms for IPOs
articles.summary: The market regulator Sebi has granted approval for eight companies to proceed with their initial public offerings. The list includes Vedanta Group's Sterlite Electric and Birla-led Svatantra Microfin. The move comes as over 70% of 2026 listings continue to trade above their issue prices.

articles.headline: Adani Group seeks approval for domestic airline sector investment
articles.summary: The Adani Group is requesting government permission to invest in airlines to complement its existing airport operations. CFO Robbie Singh stated the move would facilitate the development of the aviation sector, noting that India needs a tenfold increase in flight capacity to meet future travel demand.

articles.headline: HSBC India asks finance staff to move to 3 hubs
articles.summary: HSBC India is consolidating its finance support functions in Bengaluru, Gurugram, and Chennai, asking employees in Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Pune to relocate. This is part of efforts to simplify operations.

articles.headline: Most exports miss out on FTA gains: RBI Guv
articles.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated only 20-30% of eligible Indian exports avail FTA tariff benefits, urging MSMEs to leverage concessions and focus on quality and standards.

articles.headline: India spends ~6-7 trn extra yearly on energy imports: Tarun Kapoor
articles.summary: India's high dependence on oil and gas imports costs ~6-7 trillion annually. Advisor Tarun Kapoor stressed citizen's role in cutting avoidable fuel consumption.

articles.headline: Big-ticket capital books into India’s hospitality sector
articles.summary: India's hospitality sector sees rising institutional capital, with investments projected to reach $1.1 billion by CY26, up 94% from 2025. Marquee investors are backing branded hotel assets.

articles.headline: Tata Sons listing, EGM on Nov 30 board meet plan
articles.summary: Tata Sons' November 30 board meeting may discuss stock exchange listing and restructuring. An EGM will later address listing and Chandrasekaran's reappointment.

articles.headline: Trai extends use of 1601-series to consumer services
articles.summary: Trai extended the use of the 1601-numbering series for consumer-facing services like e-commerce and airlines to prevent fraud and impersonation by legitimate callers.

articles.headline: Amazon India workers protest in 25 cities
articles.summary: Amazon workers protested in 25 cities, raising concerns over low wages, precarious contracts, safety, and social security. The company claims fair pay and compliance with laws.

articles.headline: MINI eyes 70% India sales growth in 2026, sees EV share at 20%
articles.summary: MINI expects India sales to surge over 70% in 2026, driven by localisation and network expansion. EVs are projected to be 15-20% of sales.

articles.headline: SAP’s anticipated global layoffs may hit 1K roles in India
articles.summary: SAP's anticipated global layoffs of nearly 10,000 people may impact about 1,000 roles in India, analysts estimate, driven by AI automation and restructuring.

articles.headline: Japan’s Jera in talks with Meta, Anthropic to build data centres
articles.summary: Japan's Jera is in talks with Meta, Anthropic, and other tech giants to build data centres near power plants, aiming to accelerate AI infrastructure development.

articles.headline: Poland, Palantir sign $300 mn deal to use AI for defence
articles.summary: Poland will use AI software from Palantir Technologies for defence investments, bucking a trend of reducing reliance on US technology. The five-year deal is valued at $300 million.

articles.headline: IBM ends US visa sponsorship for most roles in consulting unit
articles.summary: IBM is discontinuing US visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles, impacting Indian staff, as US firms face pressure over work visa practices.

articles.headline: Rapido eyes deeper smaller city expansion after SC’s bike-taxi ruling
articles.summary: Ride-hailing platform Rapido plans deeper expansion in smaller cities following the Supreme Court's bike-taxi ruling, which provides regulatory clarity and is expected to boost adoption.

articles.headline: NITI Aayog moots ways to cut capital goods imports
articles.summary: NITI Aayog is assessing India's import dependence in capital goods and preparing policy recommendations to reduce it, focusing on R&D and regulatory measures.

articles.headline: Apple’s retail presence crosses 75K sq ft with Hyderabad debut
articles.summary: Apple India has leased 12,000 sq ft for its seventh store in Hyderabad, increasing its retail footprint to 77,912 sq ft across the country. The new store opens December 10.

articles.headline: Volkswagen drags Mercedes, BMW into $1.2 bn import tariff fight
articles.summary: Volkswagen told an Indian court that rivals Mercedes-Benz, BMW, and Kia import parts similarly, as it fights a $1.2 billion tax demand over alleged tariff evasion.

articles.headline: Adani group eyes $24 bn capex in FY27: CFO Singh
articles.summary: Adani Group plans around ~2.2 trillion ($23.72 billion) in capex in FY27, including $10 billion in data centres over four years, CFO Jugeshinder Singh announced.

articles.headline: RBI tells banks to speed up MSME loans, cut reliance on collateral
articles.summary: RBI urged banks to expedite MSME credit sanctions, reduce collateral reliance, and use digital channels. The Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and TReDS were highlighted.

articles.headline: Hit-and-run deaths rose 64% in a decade
articles.summary: Hit-and-run deaths in India increased by 64.3% from 20,709 in 2015 to 34,030 in 2024, despite a slight dip in cases. The problem remains significant.

articles.headline: RBI for customer consent on cards
articles.summary: RBI mandates explicit customer consent, authenticated via AFA, for registering or replacing tokenised cards with merchants, preventing pre-selected or default options.

articles.headline: White-label ATM operators can now buy cash directly from issue offices
articles.summary: RBI allowed white-label ATM operators to buy cash directly from issue offices, in addition to sourcing from banks, potentially easing replenishment and expanding rural access.

articles.headline: Nomura raises RBI rate-hike call to 50 bps
articles.summary: Nomura raised its RBI December policy rate hike forecast to 50 bps from 25 bps, citing a sharper food price increase. Bank of Baroda also expects a 25 bps hike.

articles.headline: K’taka issues show-cause notice to Indian Oil terminal
articles.summary: Karnataka issued a show-cause notice to an Indian Oil terminal in Bengaluru over discrepancies in ethanol-petrol blending, citing tests showing over 20% ethanol.

articles.headline: Pakistan’s space capability improving with China’s help: CDS Subramani
articles.summary: CDS Gen N S Subramani stated Pakistan's space capability is improving with China's help, which must be factored into India's strategic calculus.

articles.headline: Strobe Talbott, architect of India-US ties post Pokhran-II, dies at 80
articles.summary: Strobe Talbott, former US Deputy Secretary of State and key architect of India-US relations post-1998 nuclear tests, died at 80. He played a crucial role in bridging ties.

articles.headline: China-Russia-US in Shenzhen: Why it matters
articles.summary: The trilateral summit suggests a bipolar US-China condominium, with Russia less influential, creating a challenging geopolitical landscape for India. It impacts regional stability.

articles.headline: Bihar’s Bahubali fixation
articles.summary: The article discusses the persistent influence of 'Bahubalis' (strongmen) in Bihar politics, highlighting how criminal backgrounds do not hinder electoral success, impacting governance and societal issues.

articles.headline: IPO will damage Tata soul
articles.summary: The article argues that an IPO for Tata Sons could damage its 'soul' and culture, citing examples of leadership behaviour and the impact of shareholder capitalism on corporate identity.

articles.headline: IT, bank heavyweights drag mkts down 1%
articles.summary: Nifty 50 fell 1.07% and Sensex lost 1.17% on Friday, impacted by rising crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions. IT and bank stocks were major drags.

articles.headline: Small, midcap funds retain folio lead despite fall in inflows
articles.summary: Small and midcap funds continue to dominate active equity folio additions, though overall inflows declined in October. Experts cite growth expectations and relative performance.

articles.headline: Retail investors must be cautious on FPI picks
articles.summary: Analysts advise retail investors to scrutinize FPI stock purchases, considering pre-IPO capital and potential selling pressure. Tracking promoter stake changes is also recommended.

articles.headline: Facing a gold loan auction? Know all your options
articles.summary: The article outlines steps for borrowers facing gold loan auctions, including understanding notices, verifying valuations, attending auctions, and claiming surplus refunds. Legal advice is recommended.

articles.headline: Pet insurance: What is covered and why claims may get rejected
articles.summary: Pet insurance covers illnesses, accidents, and consultations, but exclusions like pre-existing conditions and waiting periods can lead to claim rejection. Careful policy review is essential.

articles.headline: IndiGo stock gains altitude, but oil, geopolitics and rupee remain key monitorables
articles.summary: IndiGo stock is up 22% in a month. While fuel costs and rupee have eased, oil prices and geopolitics remain key monitorables. The airline has strong cash and a large aircraft order book.

articles.headline: The boy who died in Harry Potter gets a licence to survive (and kill)
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson, known for playing characters facing death like Cedric Diggory and Batman, takes on the iconic role of James Bond, navigating a changing definition of cinematic heroism.

articles.headline: Tourism hotspot Goa may feel the chill this winter
articles.summary: Goa's air passenger traffic declined 9% Y-o-Y in H1FY27, with fewer flights scheduled for Nov-Dec. Higher airfares and competing destinations may impact demand.

articles.headline: 100 Indian chess grandmasters mask financial squeeze
articles.summary: Despite 100 Indian GMs, upcoming players face financial strain for travel and coaching, with limited support from sponsors and governments compared to established names.

articles.headline: Belonging: A Journey of Love by Sonia Gandhi
articles.summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging' recounts her life in India, her family's challenges, and her political journey. It offers insights into her personal and public life.

articles.headline: SEBI proposed tenure curbs may trigger leadership changes at NSE, BSE
articles.summary: Proposed SEBI regulations capping the tenure of heads at Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs) to 15 years could lead to leadership exits at India's top bourses. Current NSE CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan and BSE MD Sundararaman Ramamurthy may be affected by 2027 if the rules are implemented. The move aims to prevent concentration of decision-making power and ensure professionalized management.

articles.headline: Nifty ends winning streak as crude oil prices approach $100 barrel
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices snapped a four-week winning streak on Friday as rising global crude oil prices and a weakening rupee dampened investor sentiment. The Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex both fell over 1% as Brent crude climbed toward $98. The rupee hit an all-time low of 93 against the US dollar, driven by concerns over potential supply disruptions in West Asia and persistent inflation.

articles.headline: CERT-In warns of security vulnerabilities in WhatsApp for various platforms
articles.summary: The Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a high-severity warning regarding multiple vulnerabilities in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business. These flaws could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or bypass security restrictions on Android, iOS, Windows, and Mac systems. Users are advised to update to the latest versions to mitigate risks of unauthorized data access.

articles.headline: Adani Group plans IPO for airport business by fiscal year 2028
articles.summary: Adani Group CFO Jugeshinder Singh announced plans to list the conglomerate's airport business by FY28. The group intends to invest $140 billion over the next five years across infrastructure and energy sectors. The airport division, which currently generates about 60% of its revenue from non-aeronautical sources, is expected to see significant growth as India's air travel demand increases.

articles.headline: Gold share in India’s forex reserves falls below 14 percent
articles.summary: The share of gold in India's total foreign exchange reserves has dropped to 13.98%, its lowest level since early 2025. This decline is attributed to a sharp correction in international gold prices, which fell to approximately $3,884 per ounce. Despite the drop in value, the physical holdings of the Reserve Bank of India remained stable at roughly 880.18 tonnes as of late 2026.

articles.headline: Indian Oil Corporation to invest 800 crore in Vadodara project
articles.summary: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) is moving forward with a ₹800 crore investment to establish a new petrochemical facility at its Gujarat refinery in Vadodara. The project will focus on a Benzene, Toluene, and Xylene (BTX) unit, which provides essential feedstocks for various chemical products. The facility is expected to be commissioned within the next three years to meet rising demand.

articles.headline: BMW India targets 20,000 unit sales in 2026 despite price hikes
articles.summary: BMW Group India aims to cross the 20,000-unit sales milestone in 2026, supported by an expanded EV portfolio and new MINI models. The luxury carmaker also announced price increases of 2% to 4% effective January 2027 to offset currency fluctuations and rising input costs. The company notes that EVs now account for nearly 30% of its sales, with demand growing in non-metro markets.

articles.headline: Uppal Brewers & Distillers targets 100% volume growth for fiscal 2027
articles.summary: Uppal Brewers & Distillers (UBD) expects to double its sales volume in FY27, reaching 70,000 cases. The growth strategy includes expanding its premium whiskey brand, Soorahi, into new markets like Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka. The company is also exploring external funding of up to ₹100 crore over the next year to support its expansion and marketing efforts across India.

articles.headline: Jewellery sales lead retail growth during Indian festival season
articles.summary: A report by the Retailers Association of India (RAI) shows that the jewellery category recorded the strongest growth at 12.2% during the 2026 festival season. Overall retail sales grew by 9.2%, with North India leading the gains. While high gold prices initially slowed demand, consumer interest shifted toward lighter jewellery and gold coins toward the end of the season.

articles.headline: Rane Madras seeks to reduce revenue dependence on Maruti Suzuki
articles.summary: Auto component manufacturer Rane (Madras) is implementing a diversification strategy to reduce its reliance on Maruti Suzuki, which currently accounts for 85% of its steering business revenue. The company plans to bring three new international carmakers into its portfolio by FY29. It has committed ₹300 crore in capital expenditure for FY27 to support its expansion into new product lines.

articles.headline: S&P Global Ratings downgrades Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and JLR
articles.summary: S&P Global Ratings has lowered its credit ratings for Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) to 'BBB-'. The downgrade is attributed to weak sales performance, substantial investment requirements, and mounting cash outflows at JLR. The rating agency notes that JLR's lower-than-expected operating performance has impacted the company's overall financial health.

articles.headline: Britannia Industries CMO Amit Doshi resigns after brief tenure
articles.summary: Amit Doshi, the Chief Marketing Officer of Britannia Industries, has resigned from his position just months after joining the company. According to a regulatory filing, Doshi will be relieved of his duties by December 9, 2026. The company has not yet named a successor for the role, and Doshi plans to pursue an opportunity outside the organization.

articles.headline: India-US trade agreement nearing final conclusion says Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that a trade agreement between India and the US is in its final stages of negotiation. The deal could provide Indian exporters with a competitive edge over some Asian nations that face higher US tariffs. While some details on reciprocal tariffs are still being finalized, Goyal expressed optimism about reaching a formal conclusion soon.

articles.headline: Government evaluates compute support for AI inferencing under IndiaAI Mission
articles.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is considering expanding its IndiaAI Mission to include support for AI inferencing. While current efforts focus on providing GPU access for model development, Secretary S. Krishnan noted that inferencing is critical for scaling AI solutions. The move aims to help startups and research institutions deploy AI models more efficiently.

articles.headline: US reciprocal tariffs impact sensitive Indian export sectors like textiles
articles.summary: Recent US Section 301 reciprocal tariffs have hit Indian exports in gems, jewellery, textiles, and minerals. Shipments of pearls and semi-precious stones fell over 48% in the first half of the fiscal year, while textile and apparel exports also saw declines. Despite these challenges, some sectors like electrical machinery and iron products recorded growth during the same period.

articles.headline: Coal share in power generation hits 70 percent amid El Nino
articles.summary: India's reliance on coal for power generation reached a six-month high of 70.16% in October 2026. This surge was driven by increased demand for cooling due to high temperatures and a drop in renewable energy output from wind and hydro sources. Data from the Coal Ministry shows that coal remains the dominant source of electricity as El Nino impacts weather patterns and rainfall.

articles.headline: Ujjwala Yojana reduced household PM2.5 emissions by 15 percent
articles.summary: A study by the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW) found that the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana has helped reduce particulate matter (PM2.5) emissions from Indian households by 15% in FY26. By providing LPG connections to millions of rural families, the scheme has mitigated the health risks associated with traditional solid fuels, although refill rates remain a challenge.

articles.headline: India's foreign exchange reserves fall by 4.4 billion dollars
articles.summary: India's forex reserves decreased by $4.443 billion to $700.898 billion for the week ending November 20, 2026. The decline was largely due to a $14.2 billion drop in foreign currency assets, although gold reserves saw a slight increase of $4.095 billion. This marks the second consecutive week of decline for the country's total reserves according to Reserve Bank of India data.

articles.headline: Indian Bank to raise 2,500 crore via Additional Tier 1 bonds
articles.summary: The board of Indian Bank has approved a proposal to raise ₹2,500 crore through the issuance of Basel III-compliant Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds. The capital raise will be executed in one or more tranches during the current financial year, subject to regulatory approvals. The move is intended to strengthen the public sector lender's capital base and support its growth plans.

articles.headline: Nepal Prime Minister's visit signals new impetus for Indo-Nepal relations
articles.summary: Nepal PM Balendra 'Balen' Shah's first official visit to India has focused on resetting diplomatic and economic ties. Key discussions included a major development assistance package for Nepal worth ₹15,000 crore and the resolution of long-standing boundary disputes. Both nations expressed a commitment to a 'future-oriented partnership' focused on energy, connectivity, and education.

articles.headline: FCNR deposits and remittances support India balance of payments
articles.summary: India's balance of payments for the first half of the year was supported by steady inflows from FCNR(B) deposits and a $77.7 billion surge in remittances. Despite a trade deficit of $176.1 billion caused by rising oil prices, the capital account remained resilient. The Reserve Bank of India notes that external borrowings by Indian companies have also contributed to stabilizing the BoP.

articles.headline: Government tightens rules for electric vehicle recycling and steel scrap
articles.summary: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has revised rules for End-of-Life Vehicles (ELVs) to ensure steel scrap is sourced only from registered vehicle scrappage facilities. This amendment prevents automakers from using non-vehicle scrap to claim recycling credits. The move aims to formalize the recycling sector and improve the environmental impact of vehicle disposal.

articles.headline: Graphite electrode demand expected to rise as global capacity shrinks
articles.summary: HEG Chairman Ravi Jhunjhunwala predicts a rise in demand for graphite electrodes as several plants in the US, Europe, and Japan close down. The global market is expected to grow by 1.50 lakh tonnes over the next few years. HEG is positioning itself to capture this growth by investing ₹2,200 crore in a new facility in Madhya Pradesh to produce specialized electrode materials.

articles.headline: Shriram Finance CFO warns MSME loans carry higher risk than gold
articles.summary: Parag Sharma, CFO of Shriram Finance, noted that lending to MSMEs currently poses a greater risk to financial institutions than gold-backed loans. While gold loans are secured by a stable asset, MSME segments are more vulnerable to economic volatility and credit risks. Financial experts highlighted the need for rigorous monitoring of small business portfolios to manage potential defaults.

articles.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields shares slip 2.6 percent on stock market debut
articles.summary: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) made a disappointing debut on the stock exchanges on Friday, with its shares closing at ₹132.50, down 2.6% from the issue price of ₹136. The company is the third Coal India subsidiary to go public and is the largest coal-producing firm in India by volume. Analysts suggest the tepid response reflects investor caution regarding long-term coal demand.

articles.headline: SEBI warns investors against relying on IPO grey market premiums
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has issued a warning to retail investors against using unregulated grey market premiums (GMP) as a basis for IPO investment decisions. SEBI noted that GMP values are often manipulated by brokers and do not reflect the actual fundamentals of a company. The regulator emphasized that investors should rely only on official prospectus data.

articles.headline: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India and Vietnam
articles.summary: Ongoing worker protests and political instability in Bangladesh have prompted major fashion retailers like Zara and H&M to shift their manufacturing orders to India and Vietnam. Bangladesh’s garment industry has lost over $400 million in production recently. Indian exporters have reported a significant surge in inquiries and orders as brands seek more stable supply chain alternatives.

articles.headline: Volkswagen urges higher scrutiny of rivals' car part imports in India
articles.summary: In a legal dispute over a $1.2 billion tax claim, Volkswagen has told an Indian court that its rivals Mercedes-Benz and BMW should also face scrutiny for their car part import practices. Volkswagen argues it has been unfairly targeted with higher tariffs while competitors use similar assembly methods. The court will decide on the matter of import duty classifications on Monday.

articles.headline: HSBC reorganizes India support roles leading to job shifts for hundreds
articles.summary: HSBC is consolidating its support functions in India, moving roles from various hubs to centralized locations in Chennai, Gurugram, and Bengaluru. While the bank is offering relocation options to affected employees, the reorganization is expected to impact hundreds of positions. The move is part of a broader effort to streamline global operations and accelerate the use of AI.

articles.headline: India milk production reaches 253 million tonnes in 2025-26
articles.summary: India's milk production grew by 2.4% to reach 253.81 million tonnes during the 2025-26 fiscal year. Tamil Nadu recorded the highest growth rate at 6.59%, while Uttar Pradesh remained the largest producer overall. The increase is attributed to better animal health services and government initiatives. Per capita milk availability in India has also risen to 492 grams per day.

articles.headline: IIT Madras extends BTech internship period to six months
articles.summary: IIT Madras has announced a new curriculum change that extends the mandatory internship period for BTech students from two months to six months. The initiative aims to provide students with deeper industry exposure and better prepare them for the job market. Over 30 companies have already signed up to offer these extended internships starting in the 2027 academic year.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines to mandate portal for unclaimed financial assets
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India has refused a plea to order a new unified portal for all unclaimed financial assets, stating that the RBI's UDGAM portal already serves this purpose. The court noted that several regulatory measures are in place to help legal heirs identify and claim assets like bank deposits and mutual funds. The bench emphasized that existing systems are being improved.

articles.headline: Air India issues fuel-saving guidelines to pilots to cut costs
articles.summary: Air India has urged its pilots to adopt specific fuel-saving measures, such as single-engine taxiing and better descent planning, to reduce operational expenses. The airline noted that fuel costs account for up to 40% of its operating budget. While the guidelines are advisory, pilots are encouraged to prioritize efficiency to help the carrier navigate financial challenges.

articles.headline: TRAI amends telecom regulations to streamline connectivity and interconnection
articles.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has updated regulations governing interconnection between telecom players to improve service efficiency. The new rules require service providers to enter into agreements within 15 days and set penalties for delays in providing connectivity. These measures are intended to reduce disputes and ensure better network quality for consumers.

articles.headline: Cabinet clears Bill for women’s reservation and delimitation of seats
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has cleared a Constitution Amendment Bill to implement 33% women's reservation and increase Lok Sabha seats to 850 through delimitation. The move aims to freeze the relative share of state representation until 2051. While the DMK and NCP have expressed conditional support, concerns remain regarding the impact on southern states that successfully controlled population growth.

articles.headline: India-U.S. trade deal nearing culmination, says Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal announced that a trade agreement between India and the United States is close to completion. Speaking in Mumbai, Goyal noted that the pathway for finalizing the deal is taking shape after progress on previously stalled issues. He highlighted India's ability to maintain investor confidence despite global trade disruptions and tariff uncertainties.

articles.headline: Former CJI Gavai alleges bias in recent judicial selections
articles.summary: Former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai wrote to President Droupadi Murmu alleging that recent judicial recommendations by the Collegium disregard principles of merit and inclusivity. He claimed a specific community is being favored while candidates from marginalized sections are being excluded, citing specific instances of High Court Chief Justice transfers as evidence of this trend.

articles.headline: RBI reduces daily CRR maintenance requirement to 90% for banks
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has lowered the minimum daily maintenance of the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) from 99% to 90%, effective December 1. The move is designed to provide liquidity relief to the banking system, which has faced tightening conditions and a shift to deficit recently. The overall CRR rate remains unchanged at 4.50%, with the measure aimed purely at operational flexibility.

articles.headline: Union cabinet clears fresh delimitation-linked women’s reservation bill
articles.summary: The Union cabinet approved a revised women's reservation bill that links quotas to delimitation. The bill includes amendments to ensure no state loses Lok Sabha seats, with a projected 50% increase in total seats. The legislation is expected to be introduced during a special parliamentary session next week.

articles.headline: RBI Governor urges MSMEs to leverage lower tariffs under trade pacts
articles.summary: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das has encouraged Indian MSMEs to expand into global markets by utilizing the benefits of India's Free Trade Agreements (FTAs). Currently, only 20-30% of small businesses utilize FTA tariff benefits due to a lack of awareness. The Governor emphasized that diversifying into exports could help MSMEs scale and improve their long-term financial stability.

articles.headline: Tata Sons board to meet Monday after High Court denies relief
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court refused to grant interim relief to Tata Trusts in their plea to restrain the Tata Sons board from acting on resolutions. The decision allows the board to proceed with a meeting on Monday to discuss several matters, including the proposed initial public offering of Tata Sons. The court has scheduled the next hearing on the matter for January 21, 2027.

articles.headline: SEBI investigates Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal over minority shareholder rights
articles.summary: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has raised concerns regarding minority shareholder protection in Tata Steel's proposed acquisition of a 26.6% stake in APL Apollo Tubes. The regulator is scrutinizing the ₹15,510 crore deal to ensure it does not bypass takeover code requirements. SEBI has extended the deadline for the open offer details to December 8 to allow for further review of the terms.

articles.headline: Interoperability in AA network now from Dec 1
articles.summary: The RBI has advanced the deadline for interoperability in the account aggregator (AA) network to December 1 from December 31. Interoperability will now go live on the same day as the network's new pricing model.

articles.headline: RBI restores 90% daily CRR requirement as liquidity tightens
articles.summary: The RBI will restore the minimum 90% daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) by banks effective December 1, 2026, amid tight financial conditions. This will release ~50,000 crore into the banking system.

articles.headline: Forex reserves decline by $4.4 bn to $700.9 bn on fall in gold prices
articles.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion in the week ended November 20. Gold reserves declined by $4.10 billion to $94.52 billion.

articles.headline: FTA utilisation faces awareness, compliance issues: Experts
articles.summary: Experts cite limited exporter awareness, procedural hurdles, and difficulties meeting overseas standards for low FTA benefit utilisation in India, especially among MSMEs.

articles.headline: Swiggy Instamart cuts 340 roles to prioritize AI and automation
articles.summary: Swiggy's quick commerce division, Instamart, has laid off approximately 340 employees as it shifts its focus toward generative AI and automation. The company stated the move is part of a broader strategy to streamline operations and enhance efficiency. Affected employees will receive severance packages and support for outplacement as the firm integrates more automated systems.

articles.headline: RBI allows debit holds on ‘highly suspicious’ transactions
articles.summary: RBI allows banks to hold debit transactions deemed highly suspicious, implementing a uniform procedure for actions, including those linked to money mule activity.

articles.headline: TVS Motor launches Armado cargo tricycle for commercial mobility
articles.summary: TVS Motor Company has introduced the Armado, a cargo tricycle powered by a 200cc oil-cooled engine, to target the last-mile delivery and commercial transport segments. The vehicle features a 1-tonne payload capacity and a five-speed manual transmission. This launch marks TVS's entry into the globally competitive cargo tricycle market, with plans for exports to Latin America and ASEAN.
